name: Lingaraj Temple
century: 11th Century CE (Somavamsi Dynasty, King Jajati Keshari)
description: 55-meter towering curvilinear Sri Mandir deula, sprawling compound of 150 subsidiary shrines, laterite compound wall, and sacred Bindu Sagar tank context.

hotspots.title: 55m Curvilinear Shikhara (Sri Mandir)
hotspots.description: Rising 55 meters, the deula is divided into five vertical facets (pancharatha) with vertical miniature temple motifs (angashikharas) soaring to the crowning amalaka.
hotspots.architectural_significance: Widely regarded by architectural historians as the finest and most complete expression of Kalinga sacred architecture.

hotspots.title: Pyramidal Jagamohana & Natamandira
hotspots.description: Stepped pyramidal roof (pidha deula) featuring finely carved gargoyles, balustraded windows, and friezes of celestial musicians.
hotspots.architectural_significance: Flawless four-hall axial sequence (Deula, Jagamohana, Nata Mandapa, Bhoga Mandapa) aligned east-to-west.

hotspots.title: Ekamra Compound & Subsidiary Shrines
hotspots.description: Massive laterite stone compound wall (Kurma Pacheri) measuring 520 ft by 465 ft sheltering 150 individual shrines including the sacred Parvati Temple.
hotspots.architectural_significance: Living pilgrimage ecosystem preserved continuously for over a millennium.

sources.title: Ekamra Kshetra Heritage Masterplan & ASI Bhubaneswar Circle
sources.source: Architectural Heritage Mapping of Ancient Temples of Bhubaneswar
sources.attribution: Ekamra Heritage Project, ASI & Govt. of Odisha

reconstruction_notes: Authorized exterior perimeter and architectural skyline reconstruction derived from Ekamra Kshetra Heritage Project spatial records. Preserves precise Kalinga proportion ratio (1:4 deula to jagamohana).
surrounding_environment: Ancient Ekamra Kshetra heritage precinct, red sandstone laterite walls, and Bindu Sagar lake
